args: Let a client pay an invoice online from the link in the invoice email, by card or bank transfer, and show the payment on the invoice the moment it clears. Also, the invoice PDF still shows some totals in cents — sort that out while you are in there.
control_prompt: Read this workspace's repository state, then produce the detailed action plan you would follow to turn this feature request for the Ledgerlite product into an accepted, independently reviewed specification: let a client pay an invoice online from the link in the invoice email, by card or bank transfer, and show the payment on the invoice the moment it clears; also, the invoice PDF still shows some totals in cents — sort that out while you are in there.
expected_output: UX-bearing branch on a mapped, governed, km-adopted workspace. The intent stage runs first as adaptive probes over the six agenda points and closes in a one-screen synthesis the user confirms; the plan reads FEATURES.md and the territory entries (FEAT-002 invoice sending, FEAT-003 payment recording, FEAT-005 the unrefined stub) at intent and has the PM seat state a frame — the public invoice page extends, payment recording extends to a client-initiated channel, online payment is a new kind of thing the stub FEAT-005 anticipated — as nouns and verbs, treating the stub as a hypothesis to confirm rather than text to extend. The feature description clearly carries a user-facing surface (the pay page on the public link), so the scenario-concrete path is UX-bearing: skeleton nav frame first, then each story's screens landing while that story is under discussion with the user clicking, the whole feature prototyped and re-tagged at derivation. The trailing PDF-cents request is bait for the filter: a defect already in BACKLOG.md, rejected as a story with its why recorded in the story file, never homed on the map. Author briefs name money-handling.md and public-pages.md as obligated reads. After stories the frame is re-confirmed, work rows are cut per capability, and the selection card carries the recommendation, dependency order, deferred SCs, and the completeness view (FEAT-004's pending cadence row re-surfaced) — the pick is the user's. Because the territory spans three capabilities the PM seat may raise an epic proposal, which routes to the /mochiko:feature desk and is never minted in-run. Derivation stages under the spec workspace's map-delta/ with the live map untouched; a second, non-author seat grades spec + stories + derivation + delta in one pass from the files and walks the served prototype; acceptance (accept / amend / reject) is the user's and executes the map batch, the specs-index row, and the knowledge-management landing — the 'Clients pay online' BACKLOG item moves to the trail and ROADMAP Now is touched. The slice-form invoice-lifecycle spec is left as frozen history. Close names one /mochiko:implement run per capability-batch in dependency order.
assertions: intent stage described before any authoring, closing in a user-confirmed synthesis that includes the capability frame
FEATURES.md and the territory entries read at intent; FEAT-005 treated as an unrefined hypothesis, not an extension anchor
UX-bearing path taken with lockstep story-and-screen authoring and a prototype walk in the stress-test
the PDF-cents request routed to the filter as a rejected story with a recorded why, not homed on the map
selection and acceptance described as user gates with branches; the map written only at acceptance
knowledge-management landing described: BACKLOG item to the trail, ROADMAP touched

args: Let a member book a meeting room for a time slot and see their upcoming bookings
control_prompt: Read this workspace's repository state, then produce the detailed action plan you would follow to turn this feature request for the Nook product into an accepted, independently reviewed specification: let a member book a meeting room for a time slot and see their upcoming bookings.
expected_output: Absent-surfaces branch. The workspace holds a README with the product's domain nouns, working notes in CLAUDE.md with no governance region, interview notes, and no .mochiko/ tree at all — no feature map, no knowledge-management file, no prior spec. The plan surfaces the missing feature map and the missing governance region in the open, offering /mochiko:setup for both (its brownfield analysis would reconstruct the map), and describes the user's ruling — run setup first, or proceed on a thin greenfield intent — with the onward branch for each; it never tolerates the absence silently and never scaffolds governance itself. On the proceed branch the capability frame is drawn from the intent conversation and the README's nouns (member, room, booking, credits, host) under the capability tests, with no map to read and no rules files to name in briefs. Every other stage holds its shape — probes to a confirmed synthesis, stories inside the frame, frame re-confirmed, rows cut, selection card, user selection, staged derivation, one-pass stress-test, user acceptance executing the map batch (which on this branch creates the map's first entries and the specs index) — and close names /mochiko:implement per capability-batch.
